note: Steps of the plan, by milestone. gather.py keeps a 'done' or 'done-emu' step only while every pull request it names is merged with CI passing on the commit that brought it into main; otherwise it drops the step to 'review' or 'progress' and says why. The tag of each step (merged, in review, in progress or planned) comes from gh. 'done-emu' means checked on the host, in WASM under Node and Bun, or in headless DOSBox; nothing has run on real hardware. Milestones 0 to 6 are the working plan, with Milestone 1.5 (id m1_5) between Milestones 1 and 2, Milestone 3.5 (id m3_5) after Milestone 3 and Milestone 6 (Shell) last; Milestones 3.5 and 6 are placeholders with no start date; the order of Milestones 2 to 5 follows the restart plan in docs/POC-1-FINDINGS.md.

milestones.label: M4 · Audio
milestones.next: Merged (#99 to #108). Music and the effects both play on the Web and DOS. The level music is 'Crater Fields', Fizz 1's track used as a placeholder test song and not an official Fizz 2 track: the source (#73), the Web player (#75), the lowering to OPL2 and OPL3 (#76), the `fizz-music` stepper (#79), the DOS player (#81) and the music documents are merged, and the owner has heard the Web music. The sound effects are written: the cluck's four variants and eleven more (fzzt, fizzled, bonk, whoa!, ta-da!, the gumdrops, clunk, click, boing, the jump and crunch) in Undertone with FM voices and pitch steps, downmixed best effort to the OPL3 pair, OPL2 or the PC speaker, and wired to every rules event with the full caption table. The owner has listened to the new effects on the Web and found them good; nobody has heard them on DOS or on real hardware, and the DOS evidence is register writes and speaker steps counted under DOSBox. The milestone also brought Undertone 0.3.0 (#99), sound and caption events raised from the rules (#100), the snack-nook playground (#102), the captions (#103), effects by id (#104), the Undertone-authored effects with the Web effect picker (#105), the OPL3 pair label `FX ch5+14` (#106) and the move of the M4.5 items (#107, #108). The owner played M4 on 29 October 2026 and said it looks good in gameplay on the Web and in the DOS player. Nothing more is planned in M4 except listening on real hardware, which stays in the not-verified lists. Stereo-authored effects, the proper FM-to-OPL downmix, music from separately authored songs and the OPL tools are in M4.5.

The Web gives each voice a stereo panner and a gain, with a Classic or Enhanced button in the H panel (Enhanced by default). The rules never see the placement. nodes.label: Frame-rate policy
nodes.what: `/FPS30`, `/FPS60` and `/FPSAUTO`, and the frame-rate byte of `FIZZ2.CFG`, choose how often `/LIVE` and `/REPLAY` draw while the rules always step at 60 Hz. The pure `fizz_machine::FrameGovernor` draws every second tick at 30 Hz and, in Auto, averages 32 drawn frames on the 560 Hz clock: it moves to 30 Hz at 101 to 170% of a sixtieth of a second and to 60 Hz above 185% or below 67%, with Fizz 1's DOS port's thresholds. Both modes print `FRAMES n TICKS t RATE hz MODE m`, and `/BENCH /AUDIO` times the audio interrupt with and without music. DOSBox only: the frame costs on a real 486 are unmeasured and nobody has judged how 30 Hz looks.
nodes.evidence: tools/check-dos.sh (FRAMES lines under /FPS30, /FPS60 and Auto at 26,800 and 4,500 cycles); cargo test -p fizz-machine; docs/PLATFORM.md, The DOS runtime

nodes.label: FIZZ2.CFG version 3 and crash-safe saves
nodes.what: FIZZ2.CFG grows to 13 bytes: motion, sound placement, captions and key layout join the sound and frame-rate bytes (zero is the default, versions 1 and 2 still read, a bad value resets only its own field), with /KEEN beside /MODERN and every switch a per-field override that is never saved. The save writes FIZZ2.NEW, reads it back, deletes the old file and renames the new one (INT 21h AH=56h), and a three-byte INT 24h handler answers Fail during the save so no Abort, Retry, Fail prompt covers mode 13h. A write-protected floppy has not been tried.

nodes.what: Songs authored elsewhere arrive as Undertone modules and as OPL2 and OPL3 data (`.bin` and `.imf`, a 5-byte record format), which the stream spec imports, and a converter turns one into the other. Some OPL emulators are GPL-3.0 and the licence question is undecided; the Web game uses no OPL emulator and none is planned. About 1.2 MB for 9 songs, so only a few can ship.

nodes.label: Fizz 2 title songs A to D and Sunny Side Up
nodes.what: The Fizz 2 title songs A to D and Sunny Side Up, from separately authored material, to replace the placeholder level music where the owner chooses.
nodes.evidence: docs/MUSIC.md; docs/SOUND.md, Scores from other tools

nodes.label: The size and encoding problem
nodes.what: The nine candidate songs come to about 1.2 MB as OPL data, against a 1,100,000-byte budget for the whole executable, so a choice of songs and a tighter encoding than 5-byte records are needed before more than a few can ship.

nodes.label: The full caption table
nodes.what: Fizz 1's whole caption table on both platforms (fzzt, click - no fizz, fizzled, bonk, whoa!, ta-da!, the three gumdrops, clunk, boing and crunch) beside the chicken's own, each paired with its sound: six slots, a repeat within 11 ticks left out of the words (never out of the sound), 57 ticks of life, and the Captions setting hiding only the words. Checked in DOSBox and headless Chromium; the owner has listened to the Web sounds and found them good, DOS and hardware are unheard.
nodes.evidence: cargo test -p fizz-slice-view; docs/MANUAL.md, Captions and Sound effects; docs/SOUND.md, The effects after the cluck

nodes.label: Eleven more sound effects
nodes.what: Effects 4 to 14 (fzzt, stun, bonk, hurt, win, key, clunk, plink, boing, jump, crunch) written in Undertone from Fizz 1's patterns with FM voices and pitch steps, downmixed best effort to OPL2, the OPL3 pair and the PC speaker (7,872 bytes of OPL records and 988 of speaker divisors for all fifteen), and played for every rules event on the Web and DOS with Fizz 1's overlap rules (one DOS slot, last wins, no sound dedupe). The replay's 62 sounding events start 61 effects and `AUDIO WRITES` is 5,221, 5,242 and 10,382 (1,213 speaker steps). The owner has listened on the Web and found the effects good; DOS and hardware are unheard.
nodes.evidence: bun test web/sfx.test.ts; cargo test -p fizz-sfx -p fizz-slice-view -p fizz-present-web; bun tools/sfx/downmix.ts --check; tools/check-dos.sh (AUDIO WRITES); docs/SOUND.md

nodes.label: Effect picker on the Web
nodes.what: A list and a Play button in the H panel that plays any of the fifteen effects by id, centred and on its own, so each can be heard without playing to the event; checked against a stand-in AudioContext in headless Chromium.
nodes.evidence: tools/check-web-sfx.py (audition checks); docs/SOUND.md, Hearing the effects

nodes.label: Stereo-authored effects
nodes.what: A later option: the OPL3 pair already takes one record stream for each side, so an effect could play different content in each ear. Every effect today plays one stream on both sides.

nodes.label: Classic or Enhanced on DOS
nodes.what: The Sound placement row of the DOS Options screen chooses Enhanced or Classic, applies at once and is saved in FIZZ2.CFG; the Web has the same choice in its Placement row.
nodes.evidence: tools/check-dos.sh (OPTIONS case placement saved); docs/SOUND.md, Placing sounds

nodes.label: FM-authored effects
nodes.what: Ten of the eleven new effects use Undertone 0.3 fmVoice (fzzt, fizzled, bonk, whoa!, ta-da!, key, clunk, click, boing, crunch); the jump and the cluck are plain oscillators. The Web plays the FM and DOS plays a best-effort downmix. The owner has listened on the Web and found them good; DOS and real hardware are unheard.

nodes.label: FM-to-OPL downmix
nodes.what: A proper mapping of the FM voices (ratio, index, feedback, envelopes) to OPL operators, in place of the nearest-multiple stopgap. It waits on upstream Undertone issue 25, the companion OPL package.

nodes.label: One OPL3 stream with a skippable second bank
nodes.what: An idea to measure, not a commitment: lower the music once for OPL3 with priority tiers, so that bank 0 (at most 8 voices, channel 5 reserved for effects) is a complete arrangement and bank 1 holds only extras (doubled lines, harmonies, widening). OPL2 hardware skips bank-1 records (the record's bank bit already exists) and ignores stereo flags, so it plays centred. It needs a check that the bank-0 stream alone has no dropped notes, OPL2-compatible patches only, and it trades away the separate OPL2 lowering's smarter voice merging. First experiment: Crater Fields, comparing size and sound with today's two lowerings.

nodes.label: Compact and compress music streams, decode only the device that fits
nodes.what: An idea to measure, not a commitment: compact the records (writes that change nothing dropped, waits packed), then an LZ-style codec in the Fizz Asset Pack (compression is in `.FAP` from day one, see the M2 plan). Each device's section is compressed separately and DOS decodes only the section for the detected device at load time. A decoded song must fit the free heap (about 96 KB at 2 MB). First measurement: Crater Fields, 32 KB today.

nodes.label: Audit redundant register writes
nodes.what: A converter's output for the nine candidate songs had 26.3% of its register writes changing nothing (the write repeats the value the register already holds) and broke Fizz 2's 16-writes-per-tick cap in all 18 streams. Crater Fields has 1.1% and 0.2% in its two lowerings. The new effects downmix was not measured. Measured 2026-10-29 in a scratch experiment; the report is not committed. The audit would measure each stream, drop the redundant writes in the lowering and check the cap.
nodes.evidence: docs/MUSIC.md (the 16-write cap); measured 2026-10-29 in a scratch experiment, report not committed

nodes.label: 486 cycle budget
nodes.what: A cycle estimate against a 486DX, since DOSBox at cycles=max hides x87 cost. Fizz 1's m5/bench and its estimator are the reference.

nodes.label: Six captions in /BENCH
nodes.what: `/BENCH` also times the same busy picture with no captions and with all six slots full, and `/BENCH /AUDIO` does it while effects play over the music. DOSBox figures at a fixed 26,800 cycles a millisecond; a 486 has not been measured.

nodes.label: A real 486
nodes.what: FIZZ2.EXE on a physical 486DX with a VGA card and a real display.

nodes.label: Title, pause, options and saves
nodes.what: The title, pause and options screens, four save slots, result cards and the opening cinematic. Haptics and a debug level select come later.
